title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build from doctoral research into a strong publication record, teaching capability, academic service, research funding and long-term leadership in human rights, gender and social-justice scholarship.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. Early years emphasize doctoral research and publication; the post-Ph.D. period emphasizes postdoctoral work, teaching, grants, academic networking and independent research before progression into senior faculty roles.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish a defensible research specialization, complete doctoral work, publish and develop university-level teaching capability.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Build an independent research agenda, competitive publication record, teaching portfolio and grant/fellowship profile.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead research projects, supervise scholars, develop collaborations and take on departmental or institutional responsibilities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become a senior academic voice through major research programs, postgraduate supervision, academic leadership and public scholarship.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Build a recognizable scholarly niche while maintaining interdisciplinary methods. Add digital research, advanced empirical methods, comparative work and public scholarship so the research remains relevant to changing forms of inequality, technology, migration, labour and social policy.

Career progression
Ph.D. Researcher → Postdoctoral Researcher → Assistant Professor → Associate Professor → Professor → Senior Professor/Chair → Centre Director/Dean

Typical planning ranges are 0–3 years → 3–6 years → 6–10 years → 10–15 years → 15+ years, but academic promotion depends heavily on institution, discipline, publication quality, teaching, supervision, grants and service.
Ph.D. routes

A senior Professor should have a clearly recognized research identity, sustained publication record, successful postgraduate supervision and a history of funded or institutionally significant research. Build research centres and collaborations where appropriate, mentor early-career scholars, contribute to academic governance and maintain public-facing scholarship without sacrificing methodological rigor.
